note: THE SLASH OPT-IN ON THE LANGUAGE-NAMESPACE CLAIM (2026-10-20). Clojure spells a namespaced var `ns/name` — the same shape Go spells a module path (`encoding/json`) — and the arbiter already carries an opt-in for exactly that: the `languageNamespaceSlash` marker (incoming-rule.ts's NAMESPACE_SLASH_KEY, added 2026-10-19), which makes its `namespaceMatchOf` split on `/` as well as on `.`/`::`/`:`. Without the marker the matcher sees ONE segment under the dotted split (`js/require`), no prefix of it is in the closed language/runtime root set, and the row is UNREACHABLE by the claim: the D7 wall table called that class an INSTRUMENT GAP and said the fix was Lead-owned. The opt-in already existed, so the closure is a LANE-SIDE change — one split and one metadata key. THE POSITIVE HALF: a `js/…` target is a member of the `js` namespace, which the ClojureScript runtime provides, so it carries the claim AND the slash marker. THE NEGATIVE HALF, and it is the half that matters: a THIRD-PARTY root is still NOT claimed — `babashka.fs` is a library the project may or may not vendor, and that is a project fact a single-file analyzer cannot know; the closed list is the claim's evidence, so a root outside it carries no claim at all. The slash split must not widen the SET, only the way a root is found within it. THE TWO DIRECTIONS ARE PINNED IN OPPOSITE FORMS, because only that makes the fixture red-capable: the `expectRelationships` row for `babashka.fs/exists?` carries `meta.languageNamespace: null` (the runner's convention for 'this edge must NOT carry the key'), so it PASSES only while the row exists AND is unclaimed; the `forbidRelationships` rows carry the CLAIMED form, so they FIRE if the analyzer ever claims a third-party root.

expectRelationships.note: THE ROW EXISTS AND IS UNCLAIMED — the third-party root is outside the closed list, and the slash opt-in must not widen the list.

forbidRelationships.note: A THIRD-PARTY ROOT MUST NEVER BE CLAIMED: the closed list is the claim's evidence, and whether a project vendors a library is a project fact a single-file analyzer cannot know. This row fires if that discipline is broken.
